rule.text: - Break a large render into focused render methods named for purposeful semantic regions.

- Do not use inline event callbacks. Pass named handler references to event props. Define and bind handlers outside render; do not place arrow functions, function expressions, or `.bind(...)` calls in JSX event props or event props inside JSX spreads and input/slot property objects. Render-prop and list-mapping callbacks are not event callbacks. Static checking covers syntactically visible event values; reviewers trace aliases and callback factories that require reasoning.
- Components do not reach directly into models, transport logic, or unrelated registry services.

| Owner              | Must own                                                                                                           | Must not own                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Registry           | app-facing service lookup, lifecycle coordination, and event surfaces                                              | feature policy, startup selection, or domain behavior                                           |
| Executor           | startup sequencing and initial controller/flow selection from external facts                                       | page workflow, presentation, domain rules, or an implicit first-page policy                     |
| Model              | canonical durable/domain state, transport, persistence, serialization, normalization, and reusable domain rules    | JSX, layout, localized labels, navigation, or screen workflow                                   |
| App-facing service | a stable capability, lifecycle, caching, subscriptions, and adaptation over models/internal collaborators          | screen-specific presentation or another owner's policy                                          |
| Controller         | commands, user-facing workflow, orchestration, feature sessions, activation/mounting, and invalidation             | JSX, CSS, DOM mechanics, raw storage/transport, or duplicated canonical state                   |
| View service       | projection of controller state/actions into presentation-ready values, component choice, mounting, and event relay | domain mutation, persistence, transport, routing policy, defaults, or independent workflow      |
| React presentation | semantic JSX, MUI/DOM interaction, rendering, and genuinely transient visual state                                 | registry orchestration, model/service calls, durable mutation, URL parsing, or feature mounting |

Everything beneath a feature is private by default. Another feature must not
import its controller, view, component, model, helper, CSS, type declaration,
test support, or asset. Cross-feature collaboration must use one of these
intentional seams:
Feature-internal code and assets are private. When another feature needs a capability, expose a narrow service or promote a genuinely shared building block instead of importing feature internals.

`index.js` is the feature's runtime activation boundary. Keep most
feature-crossing imports there: it imports the owned implementations that
register services and contributions. Consumers locate app-facing capabilities
through the registry. A feature view may directly import its own concrete React
tree and private presentation helpers; that exception does not make those files
public to other features.

entries.reason: The single render method contains header, filtering, results, selected-order details, and footer regions without focused render methods.
entries.consequence: The component's independent semantic regions cannot be maintained or understood in focused units.
entries.remedy: Extract purpose-named render methods for the header, filters, results, selected-order details, and footer.

entries.reason: The button's onClick prop receives an inline arrow callback.
entries.consequence: A new event callback is created during each render and the handler is not a named reference.
entries.remedy: Bind a named refresh handler outside render and pass that handler directly to onClick.

entries.reason: The React component directly performs transport work through fetch.
entries.consequence: Presentation code owns transport behavior that should be behind a controller or service boundary.
entries.remedy: Expose loading through a controller/view-facing action and move the fetch to the owning service or model.

entries.reason: React presentation directly performs transport and writes the resulting order data into component state.
entries.consequence: The presentation layer bypasses the controller/service ownership required for application behavior.
entries.remedy: Have the component relay a named action and render controller-projected state; move transport and durable workflow ownership out of the component.

entries.reason: This file defines a non-React view-service class and contains no JSX render method.
This non-JSX view-service class has no React event props.
The file contains a view service rather than a React component.
The view service invokes model persistence and independently decides approval versus completion workflow.
entries.consequence: View projection owns domain mutation and workflow policy that belong to the controller and model/service layers.
entries.remedy: Move approval policy and save orchestration to the controller, and let the view service project controller state and actions.

entries.reason: This file defines a controller with no React render method or JSX.
This controller has no JSX event props.
The file contains a controller rather than a React component.
The controller directly uses raw browser storage.
entries.consequence: Persistence is coupled to controller workflow and bypasses model or service ownership.
entries.remedy: Move localStorage persistence behind the owning model or app-facing service and have the controller invoke its capability.

entries.reason: The component renders one small, focused button region.
The event prop receives a named handler that is bound outside render.
The presentation component delegates refresh through a supplied prop and does not call a model, transport layer, or registry.
The component renders semantic JSX and relays its event through a supplied action without owning service, transport, or workflow behavior.

entries.consequence: A private billing implementation becomes an undocumented cross-feature dependency.
entries.remedy: Expose a narrow billing capability through an intentional service seam and consume it through the registry.

entries.consequence: Feature privacy is bypassed and billing's private implementation becomes coupled to orders.
entries.remedy: Replace the re-export with a narrow published billing service capability.

entries.remedy: Register a billing-facing capability at its feature activation boundary and retrieve it through the registry.

The controller consumes a narrow billing capability supplied by the registry.
The controller locates the app-facing billing capability through the registry.
start() assumes the prices service is ready, invokes it, attaches a listener, and stop() does not remove that listener.
entries.consequence: Parallel startup can call an unready service and remounting can accumulate listeners.
entries.remedy: Move cross-service setup to ready(), retain a removable listener reference, and unregister it in idempotent cleanup.

entries.reason: start() directly gets and calls another service.
entries.consequence: The service assumes another service's initialization has completed during parallel startup.
entries.remedy: Keep start() local and move this collaboration to ready().

entries.reason: The changed listener is anonymous and stop() provides no matching cleanup.
entries.consequence: The owned listener cannot be precisely removed and can accumulate across lifecycle restarts.
entries.remedy: Store a named listener reference and remove it from the prices service in idempotent stop().

entries.reason: Cross-service lookup and listener setup occur in ready(), with corresponding listener removal in stop().
start() initializes only local state and does not call another service.
The service uses a retained bound listener and removes that exact listener during guarded cleanup.

entries.consequence: Runtime feature activation is manually maintained and can diverge from the Polylith build's included features.
entries.remedy: Import the generated Polylith feature aggregate from the application entry.
